insight: For Austria, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have been a mixed bag, with the team gaining momentum after 4 out of 8 breaks, albeit slightly, with a mean change of -0.062 minutes per break. When Austria was pressing before a break, they tended to lose momentum, with an average change of -0.160 minutes per break, and only managed to maintain their momentum once out of 5 times. In contrast, when they weren't pressing before a break, they actually gained momentum, with an average change of +0.100 minutes per break, suggesting that the team may benefit from taking a more relaxed approach before a hydration break. Overall, these statistics suggest that Austria's strategy before a break can significantly impact their performance afterwards, and that a more measured approach may be more effective in maintaining or gaining momentum.
